media.alt: AKU confers second advanced diplomas in education

content.text: The Aga Khan University-Institute for Educational Development (AKU-IED) conferred its second Advanced Diplomas to teachers and heads from various government and private schools on Saturday, July 31, 1999 at the AKU auditorium. The Chief Guest was Captain U. A. G. Isani, Chairman, and University Grants Commission of Pakistan.

Twenty-seven of the graduates were awarded the Advanced Diploma in School Management (ADISM), while fifteen received the Advanced Diploma in English Language Teaching (ADELT). Thirty percent of the head teachers in the ADISM programme were drawn from government schools and seventy percent from the private sector. Among teachers in the ADELT programme twenty percent came from government schools.
Graduates of both programmes contribute to total school improvement by working in concert with other educators and AKU-IED graduates at their home schools.

The Advanced Diploma in School Management (ADISM) is a year-long school-based programme which develops the required attitudes, skills and knowledge and the ability to critically reflect on school management practices, of principals from AKU-IED's co- operating schools.

The Advanced Diploma in English Language Teaching (ADELT) is a year-long classroom-based programme, designed to enhance content knowledge and to provide subject specialization for professional development of teachers.

AKU-IED is currently undertaking educational programs in the field of teacher education at Masters, Diploma and Certificate levels. Established in 1993 as the Aga Khan University's first programme after health sciences, AKU-IED has gained recognition as a centre of educational excellence dedicated to the professional development of teachers and overall school improvement in Pakistan and other developing countries.
